item.title: Russia Is Escalating Hybrid Attacks and Europe Has No Answer
item.description: Russia is expanding its campaign of hybrid attacks against countries that supply weapons and money to Kyiv and has caught Europe without a plan to respond.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Eglitis and Milda Seputyte

item.title: Orban’s EU Influence Comes to an Abrupt End as Cash Dries Up
item.description: Viktor Orban’s power network in his home country isn’t the only one being dismantled — a political operation the former Hungarian leader spent years building in Brussels is also coming undone.
item.dc:creator: Yurii Stasiuk

item.title: Mass Border Breach Exposes Deep Divisions in Spain’s African Exclave Ceuta
item.description: Julián Domínguez has been a doctor in Ceuta for nearly four decades.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: US Weighs More Trade Measures Against Canada
item.description: The Trump administration is discussing additional trade penalties against Canada after Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled dollar-for-dollar retaliation to new tariffs imposed by the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Renews Scrutiny of Military Procurement With Call for Tips
item.description: China’s military is asking the public to report suspected violations in the Rocket Force, extending scrutiny of a branch at the center of President Xi Jinping’s shake-up of the armed forces.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Bolivia’s Paz Names Morales as New Finance Chief With New Loans a Priority
item.description: Bolivia’s President Rodrigo Paz named Christian Andrés Morales as his new finance minister with a charge to work with international lenders to secure as much as $10 billion in new financing.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Mendoza

item.title: Trump-Backed Darline Graham Wins Senate Runoff in South Carolina
item.description: Senator Darline Graham prevailed in a Republican runoff to replace her late brother Lindsey Graham as the GOP candidate in South Carolina’s US Senate race, a victory aided by heavy support from President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: Canada Doubles Tariffs on US Steel Products up to 50% | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/25/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Ontario Premier Doug Ford says Canada should answer US tariffs “tariff for tariff and dollar for dollar,” but urges President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Mark Carney to reach a fair agreement. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX) says tariff threats should be used to open markets, lower trade barriers and expand trade—not to keep tariffs high indefinitely. Michael Faulkender, Former Deputy Secretary of the United States Treasury, says Kevin Warsh should reinforce his commitment to bringing inflation back to 2.0%, while arguing that energy-driven price pressures do not justify an interest-rate increase. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Weighs More Trade Measures Against Canada After Retaliation
item.description: The Trump administration is discussing additional trade penalties against Canada after Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled dollar-for-dollar retaliation to new tariffs imposed by the US on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Faulkender: Warsh Should Reaffirm 2% Target, Not Hike Rates
item.description: Michael Faulkender, Former Deputy Secretary of the United States Treasury, says Kevin Warsh should reinforce his commitment to bringing inflation back to 2.0%, while arguing that energy-driven price pressures do not justify an interest-rate increase. Faulkender says the $40 trillion debt threshold may have finally focused markets on rising debt-service costs and describes the Treasury’s bond-buyback program as useful, but only a “rounding error.” He also assesses Axios reporting that Marco Rubio told foreign counterparts the US is shifting from new strikes toward sanctions on Iran, including potential pressure on China over its purchases of Iranian oil. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: H-1B Visas: Why Trump Wants $103,000 Fee After Previous Policy Was Struck Down
item.description: In addition to ramping up immigration enforcement and deportations in his second term, US President Donald Trump has taken steps to overhaul the H-1B visa program. Trump argues that the H-1B, a cornerstone of the employment-based immigration system that allows US companies to hire college-educated foreigners for specialized occupations, has been exploited to displace American workers.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Kreighbaum

item.title: Sen. Ted Cruz on Canada Trade, Data Center Backlash, Clarence Thomas
item.description: US Senator Ted Cruz, a Texas Republican, discusses US-Canadian trade tensions, the backlash against data center development and the legacy of Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Burnham Urges Firms to Follow Sainsbury’s Work Offer for Youths
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham called on British firms to offer work experience to teenagers to help tackle what he called a “youth unemployment crisis”.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: California Lawmakers Oppose Insurance Fire Claims Limits
item.description: California lawmakers are lining up against Governor Gavin Newsom’s push to rewrite how the state assigns financial responsibility for wildfires sparked by equipment owned by publicly traded utilities.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Oxford and Michelle Ma

item.title: Carney Matches Trump Tariffs With 50% Tax, US Dairy, Steel
item.description: Trade talks between the US and Canada came to a halt over the weekend with new US tariffs going into effect. Now Canada has responded with counter-tariffs. Mathieu Dion explains what this all means (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent's Bond Buying "Mistake" | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/25/2026
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's mentor Stanley Druckenmiller says the Treasury's bond buying plan is a mistake. Bloomberg News Economy Editorial Director Erik Schatzker explains Druckenmiller's reasoning for calling out his mentee, and the implications of the Treasury Secretary's moves. Then, Balance of Power Co-Anchor Kailey Leinz interviews Northrop Grumman CEO Kathy Warden about the defense industry and its relationship with the US Government. Plus, Amazon's VP of Alexa and Echo Daniel Rausch about what's next for Amazon's at-home smart devices. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Trump’s Feud With Canada Became a Full-Blown Trade War
item.description: The president may not back down immediately — despite the damage it could cause to US states during the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Doug Ford Seeks Truce With Trump as Canada Doubles Steel Aluminum Tariffs to 50%
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford called for a truce in his war of words with President Donald Trump but backed Canada’s plan to retaliate against fresh US tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Shin and Thomas Seal

item.title: Iran, Oman Push Talks for ‘Interim’ Reopening of Hormuz
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his Omani counterpart Badr Albusaidi discussed an “interim framework” aimed at resuming shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a joint statement carried by the Oman News Agency, as the two sides press ahead with long-running talks over navigation through the key waterway.
item.dc:creator: Veena Ali-Khan and Arsalan Shahla

item.title: Xi Signals Defiance as US Threatens Sanctions Over Iran Help
item.description: Xi Jinping’s government is sending a message of defiance to Donald Trump over China’s economic ties with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
